facts.text: The hotel has a foot in historic Old Montreal and a finger on the pulse of the downtown scene.
facts.excerpt: With a foot in historic Old Montreal and a finger on the pulse of the downtown scene, W Montreal sits in its own unique space.

facts.text: The hotel is on Square Victoria inside the old Banque du Canada building.
facts.excerpt: The hotel is located on Square Victoria inside the old Banque du Canada building.

facts.text: The Old Port's landmarks, waterfront experiences and restaurants are within a 10-minute walk of the hotel.
facts.excerpt: historic landmarks, waterfront experiences, restaurants, and seasonal attractions are all within a 10-minute walk from W Montreal.

facts.text: To the left of the hotel are the Old Port and Notre Dame Basilica.
facts.excerpt: To the left of our hotel near downtown Montreal, discover the enchanting Old Port and Notre Dame Basilica.

facts.text: The Bell Centre is a 10-minute walk from the hotel.
facts.excerpt: the Bell Centre is a 10-minute walk (0.62 miles) for events.

facts.text: The Penthouse Corner Suite has ribbons suspended above the bed in homage to Cirque du Soleil, and the largest terrace at W Montreal.
facts.excerpt: The suite features ribbons suspended above the bed, paying homage to Cirque du Soleil, inspiring wonder and creativity. Enjoy the largest terrace at W Montreal

facts.text: The Premium Penthouse Suite has a library inspired by Montreal's Villa Maria metro station.
facts.excerpt: With its unique library inspired by Montreal’s Villa Maria metro station, this suite pays tribute to the city’s metro architecture.

facts.text: The Penthouse King Suite's island unit draws inspiration from the Biosphere, the Palais des Congres and Habitat 67.
facts.excerpt: The island unit draws inspiration from the Biosphere, the Palais des Congrès, and Habitat 67

facts.text: The Penthouse II Suite is spread over two stories.
facts.excerpt: Spread over two stories and 1,100 sq. ft.

facts.text: Each Penthouse Suite has a private terrace with views of downtown Montreal.
facts.excerpt: Each of our Penthouse Suites features a private terrace, offering stunning views of downtown Montreal.

facts.text: The Vinyl Bar has a curated collection of 3,000 records, a custom listening station and live DJ sets.
facts.excerpt: Browse a curated collection of 3,000 records handpicked by our music curator, drop the needle at the custom listening station, and vibe out to live DJ sets.

facts.text: The Retro Gaming Box offers a lineup of classic video game consoles.
facts.excerpt: The Retro Gaming Box at W Montréal takes you back to the golden age of video games with a lineup of legendary consoles

facts.text: The Living Room is a coworking space by day that turns into a bar when the day is done.
facts.excerpt: Follow the beat of our Living Room, a coworking space designed to boost focus and creativity. When the days are done, the space turns into a mingling bar.

facts.text: Tbsp. is the hotel's restaurant, combining French and Italian flavors in dishes made for sharing.
facts.excerpt: Tbsp. is our downtown Montréal restaurant where French and Italian flavors come together through generous dishes made for sharing.

facts.text: Bota Bota, a floating spa in Montreal's Old Port, is a short stroll from the hotel.
facts.excerpt: take a short stroll to Bota Bota, the iconic floating spa in Montreal's Old Port.

facts.text: Pet services include dog walking, grooming and pet birthday cakes, at an additional cost.
facts.excerpt: including dog walking, a grooming service, and even pet birthday cakes (services available at an additional cost)

facts.text: The hotel sits above a Metro station whose entrance has a classic Art Nouveau sign.
facts.excerpt: the Metro station, over which the hotel sits, even features a classic Art Nouveau sign

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes that, as with many W Hotels, late-night noise can be an issue.
facts.excerpt: As with many W Hotels, late-night noise can be an issue.

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler has heard the atrium-view rooms can get a little dark, while park-facing rooms flood with natural light.
facts.excerpt: We've heard the "atrium view" rooms can get a little dark, unlike the park-facing rooms, which flood with natural light.

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler says the hotel is in a business district, not exactly in the middle of the action, but a five-minute walk from it.
facts.excerpt: So you're not exactly in the middle of the action, but walk five minutes in any direction and you'll be in the action.
